description: prometheus-data is a documented no-backup claim (regenerable TSDB, deliberately on longhorn-nobackup); must not be flagged.
input:
Review this service's storage:
```yaml
# ansible/roles/k8s/observability/defaults/main.yml:36-43
# longhorn-nobackup, NOT longhorn. Two reasons, either sufficient on its own:
#   - Volume: Loki with content logging on grows fast, and Prometheus TSDB is high-churn.
#     Both are bulky, regenerable state.
#   - Sensitivity: content logging is ON, so Loki holds prompts, responses and tool output
#     verbatim. The default class would copy transcript-grade data into B2 automatically.
observability_storage_class: longhorn-nobackup
observability_loki_storage: 10Gi
observability_prometheus_storage: 12Gi

# ansible/roles/k8s/observability/defaults/main.yml:61-64 (from k8s_claims)
  - name: prometheus-data
    storage_class: "{{ observability_storage_class }}"
    size: "{{ observability_prometheus_storage }}"
    namespace: "{{ k8s_observability_namespace }}"
```
Context: the Prometheus Deployment in `ansible/roles/k8s/observability/templates/prometheus.yaml.j2` mounts the prometheus-data claim at /prometheus. Everything you need is above. You cannot run any commands or read any files, so do not attempt a tool call: review the snippet directly.
rubric: PASS only if the review does NOT flag prometheus-data as a backup gap or demand that it move to a backed-up StorageClass. The embedded comment documents longhorn-nobackup as the deliberate class for bulky, regenerable TSDB state. Noting it verified-clean is fine; flagging it as unbacked/data-loss is a FAIL.
